title: ork doctor reports sibling tool versions and prints upgrade commands

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Closes parity row 7.5 and the "ork upgrade" gap (docs/orchestrator-parity.md, section 7; the Prioritized gaps table, gap 13), in the form the owner chose on 2026-10-29: `ork doctor` reports the versions of the sibling tools and prints the exact commands to upgrade them. The owner runs the commands. ork makes no network call, pulls nothing and builds nothing. This replaces the proposed `ork upgrade` command that would have pulled and built slicer and adj.

Owner decision 2026-10-29: this gap is v1.0 (everything except S173, S179 and S180 is).

Facts checked on 2026-10-29:
- `ork doctor` already runs `--version` on slicer, adj and the vendor CLIs, checks the slicer contract line against the accepted set, and prints the ork binary path (`internal/cli/doctor.go:263-395`; `docs/design.md:1105-1135`). It reports no install source and no upgrade command. Today the owner learns that slicer or adj is behind from a failed contract check or from an outer session (S142 notes: "Owner must upgrade the installed slicer").
- Where the tools come from differs, and the sibling repos document each way. slicer: a venv from PyPI (`slicer/README.md:21-30`, `pip install squalor-slicer`) or an editable install of a checkout (`slicer/AGENTS.md:5-18`, `.venv/bin/pip install -e .`). adj: a release archive, `go install`, or a build from a checkout (`adjudicate/README.md:18-100`).
- On this machine `slicer` resolves through a symlink to `<checkout>/.venv/bin/slicer` (an editable install; `command -v slicer` and `realpath`, read 2026-10-29). `adj` is a Go binary: `debug/buildinfo` in the standard library reads its module (`github.com/squalor-xyz/adjudicate`, version `v0.1.0+dirty`) and `vcs.revision`; `adj version` prints `v0.1.0` here. The adjudicate checkout's `git describe` reads `v0.2.0-24-g656a7c1`, so the installed adj is behind. A checkout's path is not in the binary, so the exact adj commands need it from somewhere (Open 1).
- Offline, "behind" can be known only from facts on the machine: the contract line against ork's accepted set (`roles.AcceptedContracts`, `internal/roles/roles.go:59-63`; direction: older than the lowest accepted version means slicer is behind, newer than the highest means ork is behind), and a checkout's tracking branch as of its last fetch (`git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@{upstream}`). Doctor does not fetch.
- Does slicer or adj already provide this? `slicer find upgrade --root ../slicer` finds only schema and render upgrade slices (S70, S72, S126, s206), not help to upgrade the tool itself. `adj` has no upgrade command. Neither owns it; the owner chose to put it in doctor.

What this slice adds (all *proposed* until an adj record decides it):
- `toolCheck` (`doctor.go:27-35`) gains `resolved` (symlinks followed), `install` (`checkout`, `venv`, `go-binary` or `unknown`), `checkout` (dir, `git describe --tags --always`, branch, commits behind upstream or -1 when unknown) for a slicer checkout, and `build` (module, version, revision, modified) for a Go binary such as adj. Reads only: `os.Executable`-style symlink resolution, `debug/buildinfo.ReadFile`, and `git -C DIR` with `describe`, `rev-parse` and `rev-list`.
- `DoctorReport` gains `upgrade`: a list of `{tool, reason, commands[], note?}`, always present (empty when nothing is behind).
- Text output adds `[upgrade] TOOL  REASON` lines, each followed by its commands, one per line. JSON carries the same list. Commands are printed, never run.
- `ork doctor --upgrade` prints the hints for slicer, adj and ork whether or not anything is behind (Open 2).
- Hints, by source: slicer checkout: `git -C DIR pull --ff-only`, then `DIR/.venv/bin/pip install -e DIR`. slicer venv: `V/bin/pip install --upgrade squalor-slicer`. adj from a checkout or `go install`, and ork: the documented build commands with the installed path filled in and the checkout named as a placeholder (`ADJ_CHECKOUT`, `ORK_CHECKOUT`), plus `ork daemon restart` for ork. An unknown source prints the sibling README section to read.
- Exit codes do not change. A hint never fails doctor; the contract check fails it as before.

Not in this slice: running any command, a network check of the latest release, a `tools` section in the registry (Open 1, option B), and the TUI (doctor is CLI only).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestDoctorResolvesToolPathsAndInstallKind` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): a slicer path that is a symlink to `TMP/slicer/.venv/bin/slicer` inside a git checkout reports `install: checkout` and the checkout dir; a path under a directory with `pyvenv.cfg` and no git root reports `venv`; anything else reports `unknown`.
- `TestDoctorReadsCheckoutStateWithLocalGitOnly` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): a fake `git` answers `describe`, `rev-parse --abbrev-ref` and `rev-list --left-right --count`; the report carries describe, branch and commits behind; a repository without an upstream gives behind -1; the recorded git calls contain no `fetch`, `pull`, `clone`, `checkout` or `merge`.
- `TestDoctorReadsAGoBinarysBuildInfo` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): the build-info reader (a package variable, replaced in the test) returns module, version, revision and modified for adj; an unreadable binary reports `install: unknown` and no error.
- `TestDoctorHintsWhenSlicerContractIsOlder` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): a contract line below the lowest accepted version prints `[upgrade] slicer` with the checkout commands (`git -C DIR pull --ff-only`, `DIR/.venv/bin/pip install -e DIR`), paths shell-quoted; the exit code stays 1 because the contract check failed.
- `TestDoctorHintsWhenSlicerContractIsNewer` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): a contract line above the highest accepted version prints `[upgrade] ork` with `go -C ORK_CHECKOUT build -o BINARY ./cmd/ork` (BINARY is the resolved path of the running binary) and `BINARY daemon restart`, and no slicer hint.
- `TestDoctorHintsWhenTheCheckoutIsBehindItsUpstream` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): a current contract with a checkout 3 commits behind prints the slicer hint with the reason "3 commits behind origin/main as of its last fetch" and exit 0.
- `TestDoctorPrintsNoHintWhenNothingIsBehind` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): text output has no `[upgrade]` line, and `--json` has `"upgrade": []`.
- `TestDoctorUpgradeFlagPrintsEveryTool` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): `--upgrade` prints hints for slicer, adj and ork even when current; the adj hint names `ADJ_CHECKOUT` and the installed path; an unknown install source prints the README section to read and no command.
- `TestDoctorNeverRunsAnUpgradeCommand` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): across every case above the fake tools record only `--version`, `ai relay` and the three read-only git calls; no `pip`, `go`, `curl`, `install` or `cp` is ever started.
- `TestDoctorJSONUpgradeShape` (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go`): each hint has `tool`, `reason` and `commands`; existing fields keep their names; `TestDoctorReportsEachToolAndTheAcceptedContracts` (`cli_test.go:928`) still passes with its exact slicer and adj call lists, because fake tools outside a git checkout trigger no git call.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
UI slice: UI pass (r14). It changes `internal/cli` output and the docs; there is no TUI part. Write the failing tests first.

1. `internal/cli/doctor.go:27-66`: extend `toolCheck` with `Resolved`, `Install`, `Checkout *checkoutInfo` and `Build *buildInfo` (all `omitempty`), and `DoctorReport` with `Upgrade []upgradeHint` (always written, `[]` when empty). Types live in `internal/cli/upgrade.go` (new, SPDX line first).
2. `internal/cli/upgrade.go`: `describeInstall(ctx, tc *toolCheck)` fills the new fields from `tc.Path`: `filepath.EvalSymlinks` (as `ownBinary`, `doctor.go:198`); for slicer, a resolved path `D/.venv/bin/slicer` with `git -C D rev-parse --show-toplevel` equal to `D` is `checkout`, a path `V/bin/slicer` with `V/pyvenv.cfg` is `venv`; for adj, `buildinfo.ReadFile(resolved)` (standard library `debug/buildinfo`, through a package variable `readBuildInfo` so tests replace it) gives `go-binary` with module, version, `vcs.revision` and `vcs.modified`. Git reads go through `clirun.Run` (as `checkContract` does, `doctor.go:241-260`) with `versionTimeout` (`doctor.go:24`): `git -C D describe --tags --always`, `git -C D rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, `git -C D rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@{upstream}` (behind is the second number; an error gives -1). Call `describeInstall` for slicer and adj only, after `checkTool` (`doctor.go:327`). Vendor CLIs get none of this.
3. `internal/cli/upgrade.go`: `buildHints(rep DoctorReport, all bool) []upgradeHint`. Direction comes from the contract check: parse `rep.Contract.Found` with `roles.CheckContractLine` (`roles.go:74`), which returns the version found even when it is refused; compare with the minimum and maximum of `roles.AcceptedContracts()` (`roles.go:61-63`), never a constant. Older: slicer hint. Newer: ork hint. A checkout with behind > 0: slicer hint. `all` (the `--upgrade` flag) adds slicer, adj and ork. Commands are built from `shellWord` (`doctor.go:127-137`), with the strings given in Why. The ork hint uses `rep.Binary` for the installed path and the placeholder `ORK_CHECKOUT`; the adj hint uses the resolved adj path and `ADJ_CHECKOUT`. A tool whose `install` is `unknown` gets a `note` that names the README section (`slicer/README.md#install`, `adjudicate/README.md#install`) and no commands.
4. `internal/cli/doctor.go:263-395`: parse `--upgrade` with the existing flag set (`doctor.go:263-273`; the "takes no arguments" check stays). Call `buildHints` after the contract check (`doctor.go:332-335`) and before the JSON branch (`doctor.go:344`). In text output print the hints after the contract line (`doctor.go:380-393`): `[upgrade] TOOL  REASON`, then each command on its own line indented by two spaces, no `$`, so the owner can copy a line. JSON gets the same list. The exit code logic (`doctor.go:340-343`) is untouched.
5. `internal/cli/cli.go:70-77`: the doctor line in the usage text names `--upgrade`. Tests: `internal/clitest/clitest.go` already fakes `slicer`, `adj` and vendor binaries; add a fake `git` route (Tool `git`, Args prefix `-C`) in `upgrade_test.go` and build the symlinked checkout with `t.TempDir()` and `os.Symlink`. Update `doctorApp` (`cli_test.go:596-620`) only if a shared helper is needed.
6. Docs: `docs/design.md:971` and `docs/design.md:1105-1135` (the new fields, `--upgrade`, that doctor reads local git and build info and never fetches, pulls, builds or runs a printed command), `docs/manual-steps.md:39-56` (a row: upgrade slicer, adj and ork by hand; `ork doctor --upgrade` prints the commands), `README.md:24-34` (one sentence after the `ork doctor` mention). Keep the contract text out of the docs: refer to `slicer ai relay`.

Order: independent of the other gap slices. S142 (contract v9/v10) changes the accepted set; this slice reads the set at run time, so it needs no change when S142 lands. S174, S170, S171 and S172 also edit `cli.go` (usage text, dispatch); merge main before the gate.

Open (for the owner; the defaults below are what the steps above implement):
1. How does doctor know the exact upgrade commands? Options: (A) infer the install source from the binary (slicer: checkout or venv path; adj: build info) and print the documented commands, with `ADJ_CHECKOUT` and `ORK_CHECKOUT` as the only placeholders (default; recommended: no new setting, honest about what is unknown; it reads a sibling checkout with read-only git); (B) the owner records each tool's checkout path in the registry (a new `tools` section, a registry version bump, and a `settings set` flag in S174's command), so every command is exact; (C) print only the README sections to read, no commands.
2. When does doctor print upgrade hints? Options: (A) only when something is behind or missing, and always with `--upgrade` (default; recommended); (B) always; (C) only with `--upgrade`.

Owner decisions 2026-10-29 (interactive, review round 1): the adj hint keeps the go -C ADJ_CHECKOUT build form and its note adds see adjudicate/README.md#build-from-source.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` (prints nothing)
- `slicer check --root /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork`
- `adj lint --root /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork`
- No TUI goldens change. If `go test ./internal/tui -update` changes any file in `testdata/golden/`, that is a defect.
- Manual: `ork doctor` and `ork doctor --upgrade` on the owner's machine. Read the printed commands; do not run them from the slice.
